description: Start a video from text, a source image, or references (@Image 1, @Video 1, @Audio 1 in the prompt). Asynchronous: returns a job id; poll get_job. Corent picks the model; a model the user names in the prompt is used. Set quality "best" only when the user asks for the best quality, max_cost_cents for a budget. Photos of real people are rejected as references.

aspect_ratio.description: Shape of the clip. OMIT IT (or pass adaptive) when animating a source image, editing or extending a clip: those keep the source's own shape, so naming another is refused rather than silently ignored. Omitted for text-to-video means the model's own default (landscape).

audio.description: Ask for native SOUND. Some models render audio and some are silent. true routes only to models that actually deliver sound, so a silent model can never quietly serve the request; false prefers a silent one; omit to let Corent choose. list_models reports has_audio per video model. Use true whenever the user asks for a clip with sound, music, or speech.

end_image_url.description: The frame the clip should END on. Together with image_url this is the go-from-A-to-B / morph effect; alone it is a target to move toward.

enhance_prompt.description: false sends the prompt exactly as written.

fps.description: Frames per second, where the model offers a choice.

image_url.description: If set, animates this image as the FIRST frame instead of pure text-to-video. Use a previous clip's last_frame_url to continue from it.

max_cost_cents.description: The most this may cost, in cents. Set it when the user gives a budget or a price limit. Refused before anything is spent when no model fits under it, and never exceeded.

model.description: Pin an exact model by name, e.g. "corent-seedance-2.5" (list_models shows the menu; every name there is spelled corent-*). Never substituted; duration and resolution snap to THAT model's own menu; max_cost_cents still applies. Only for a user who insists on one exact model. list_models reports supports_reference_images, supports_video_edit, supports_video_extend and supports_last_frame per video model.

negative_prompt.description: What must NOT appear in the clip.

prompt.description: What to generate, in plain language. If the user names a model ("use seedance 2.5", "made with Veo 3.1 Fast"), leave that in the prompt: Corent uses that model when it can do the job, removes those words before rendering, and the receipt says so.

quality.description: Set "best" only when the user asks for the best or highest quality: Corent then uses its top model for the job, which costs more. Leave it out otherwise and Corent picks the model. Has no effect when `model` pins one.

reference_audio_urls.description: 1 to 10 public https audio files, @Audio 1 in the prompt, e.g. a track the clip should cut to.

reference_image_urls.description: 1 to 30 public https images the clip should keep to (a character, a product, a setting). Refer to them in the prompt as @Image 1, @Image 2 in this order. Needs a model that takes references (corent-seedance-2.5; a batch item is routed to one); cannot be combined with image_url/end_image_url. The supplier rejects photos of REAL people as references; characters generated inside Corent are accepted.

reference_video_urls.description: 1 to 10 public https clips, @Video 1, @Video 2 in the prompt: the source for an edit or extend task, or motion/style to follow. Cannot be combined with image_url/end_image_url.

resolution.description: Pixel resolution (default 720p). Higher resolutions cost more (1080p ~2.5x, 4k ~5.5x). If the chosen model tops out lower, it steps down to the closest it offers rather than refusing; the result says what was delivered.

return_last_frame.description: true also stores a PNG of the final frame and returns it as last_frame_url on the finished job, so the next clip can start exactly there (pass it as image_url). Use it to chain shots.

style.description: Optional content style hint, same vocabulary as generate_image

task.description: What to do with the references (default auto). edit changes something in @Video 1 and keeps its length: omit duration_s. extend continues @Video 1. Both need reference_video_urls and aspect_ratio omitted or adaptive. The prompt must say the intent (add, remove, replace, change; extend, continue).
